data.name: Anvitha
data.gender_notes: Anvitha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anvitha is a Sanskrit name meaning 'one who embodies grace, beauty, and compassion'. In Hindu mythology, Anvitha is often associated with the goddess Saraswati, who represents knowledge, learning, and wisdom. The name Anvitha carries the meaning “Grace, beauty, compassion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anvitha usually hope their child will grow to embody grace, beauty, compassion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizing inner beauty and compassion, Anvitha is a divine name that inspires kindness and grace.
data.etymology: Anvitha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grace, beauty, compassion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anvitha total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

vedic_reference.note: Anvitha is a Sanskrit name that means 'new beginning'. It is derived from the Sanskrit words 'anu' meaning 'new' and 'vith' meaning 'beginning'.

historical_references.reference: Anvitha is a variant of the name Anandavalli, which was the name of a revered 12th century Hindu queen of the Chola dynasty in southern India. Anandavalli was the daughter of Rajaraja Chola I and was married to Kulothunga Chola I in 1101 CE. She is known for her wisdom, beauty and exceptional piety.
historical_references.context: Hindu queen of the Chola dynasty in southern India

historical_references.reference: Anvitha also refers to the name of a celestial nymph in Hindu mythology, Anvitha Devi. She is described as the embodiment of spiritual knowledge and the goddess of wisdom and learning. The name Anvitha means 'all-knowing' or 'omniscient'.
